History:
• 37-year-old male presents with 4-day history of severe, generalized headache that began first, followed by subjective fever (temperature not measured).  
• Associated symptoms: diffuse generalized muscle aches, feels cold at times, red itchy rash now present over entire body. Rash blanches with glass test.  
• Denies photophobia, neck stiffness, nausea/vomiting, cough, coryza, ear pain, focal weakness, or paresthesias.  
• Travel: Returned from Thailand 1 week ago; multiple mosquito bites; travel companion also unwell.  
• Self-treatment: Paracetamol and ibuprofen with minimal relief.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical or surgical history reported.  
• No regular medications; uses paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) and ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) as needed.  
• No known drug allergies.  
• Immunizations, family, and social history not recorded.

Physical Examination:
(virtual consultation)  
• General: Conversing normally, no distress noted.  
• Neurologic: No focal deficits reported; denies photophobia and neck stiffness.  
• Skin: Patient-reported diffuse red, pruritic, blanching rash.  
• HEENT/Respiratory/Cardiovascular/Abdominal: Not recorded.  
• Vitals: Not recorded.

Impression:
Febrile illness with severe headache and blanching pruritic rash after recent travel to Thailand; requires urgent in-person evaluation to exclude serious tropical or neurologic infection.
Top aligned differentials:  
1. Dengue fever – fits travel, fever, severe headache, myalgias, blanching rash.  
2. Chikungunya virus infection – similar mosquito exposure; fever, headache, pruritic rash.  
3. Malaria – endemic exposure; fever and headache mandate rule-out.

Management Plan:
• Arrange urgent face-to-face assessment at GP hub today for full physical exam and vitals.  
• Anticipate blood tests: FBC/platelets, LFTs, dengue serology, malaria thick/thin film, renal profile, inflammatory markers; consider rapid antigen tests for dengue/malaria if available.  
• Possible hospital referral depending on examination and results.  
• Symptomatic relief: continue paracetamol or ibuprofen as needed, stay well-hydrated.  
• Safety-netting: Seek emergency care (A&E/EMS) if rash becomes non-blanching, develops neck stiffness, persistent vomiting, altered mental status, worsening headache, bleeding, or inability to access same-day review.

Patient Summary:
John Doe has a 4-day severe headache, subjective fever, myalgias, and diffuse blanching itchy rash after travel to Thailand with mosquito exposure. Dengue or other arboviral infection is suspected; meningitis and malaria must also be excluded. He will attend an urgent in-person review today with possible hospital referral and blood work.

Key Takeaways:
• Attend same-day GP hub for examination and labs.  
• Continue simple analgesia; monitor for any new red-flag symptoms.  
• Go to emergency services if unable to secure appointment or if condition worsens.

Next Steps:
• Complete laboratory evaluation for tropical infections and full physical exam today.  
• Consider hospital admission if thrombocytopenia, positive malaria film, concerning vitals, or meningitic signs.  
• Schedule follow-up once results available or sooner if symptoms escalate.
